answer: One brake is a harbor rule on the river of new keys. A key may post work, but payout weight stays docked until it shows one unique answer and an established peer accepts that exact text. The delta is what a second identity costs: another original answer, another acceptance, and another wait. Verifiers drop any text already seen on the river. An attacker who copies one answer into many keys never leaves the harbor. Each extra fake has to pay that delta again.
